reviewer: Codex deployment_review subagent; bounded independent read-only source and offline behavioral review
scope: Existing-demo lifecycle mutation guards, account and resource identity checks, CIDR updates and SSH configuration preservation
Runbook lifecycle, rollback, cleanup and evidence boundaries
Native backend runner manual once-only approval flow, exact-input checks, result/SEL/audit correlation, failure handling and sanitization
Native launcher runtime selection, argument forwarding and clean environment

resolved_findings.resolution: CIDR update and verification now precede start-instances. A failed update prevents compute start and local SSH/tunnel changes.
Manual delete-stack and wait now use the exact recorded full StackId ARN, binding account and deployment identity.
Dictionary keys and values are sanitized, including nested JSON strings. Sensitive-field matching uses the original key; the fixed public canonical-identity limitation field is preserved.

source_review_observations: Cloud mutations require --apply, while offline apply, status apply and cleanup-plan apply are refused. Cleanup itself remains a manual documented action.

The helper checks the fixed account, stack/instance binding, instance type, project tags, sole security-group attachment, exact TCP22 IPv4 /32 ingress and agreement with the CloudFormation parameter before operational mutation.

SSH edits change only the shared HostName line and preserve other bytes. Dedicated known-host settings and strict checking are required. Local edits use backups, concurrent-change checks and atomic replacement.

Native approvals require an explicit operator decision for the current request ID and card digest, exact trace-only JSON arguments, unchanged pending card and visible input. There is no automatic approval or persistent trust grant.
An interactive permission card during crew_denied is rejected for containment and immediately fails the run. That manual rejection does not count as Crew-denial proof.

Native success requires exact tool-call-ID and trace joins, independent MCP audit correlation, stable service identity, native SEL evidence and valid SEL chain. The canonical identity limitation is disclosed rather than inferred from a display title.
The native launcher passes arguments without shell reinterpretation and removes inherited AWS/Python environment overrides.
limitations: No cloud mutation, model request, SSH connection, login or service operation was performed during this operator-script review.

The start/failure ordering checks invoked the main function only with mocked cloud, local-file and tunnel boundaries. They do not establish successful real stop/start, changed-IP recovery or rollback.
Live native backend execution remains a separate acceptance step. Offline code checks do not establish native Crew, MCP, AWS or sandbox behavior.
Parameterized approval cards do not expose canonical MCP server/tool identity. The runner requires manual card review and does not claim display titles provide authoritative identity.

Crew denial SEL lacks a direct trace/tool-call-ID field. Its verdict uses the explicitly documented isolated session/phase correlation, plus a trace-bearing host blocked row and independent healthy MCP journal interval.
Other subagent synthetic evaluator tests were assessed through their reports and source inspection; this reviewer independently executed only the checks listed above.
